name: Week 25 Push — 55 On Purpose (Spotlight: Dips + Farmer Carry)
description:
**Warmups are baked into each block's notes as a reminder.**

Incline DB opens at **55 for all three sets** — last week it got there by accident and held; this is the deliberate run. Nothing else is stacked on top of it.

**Push press changes shape rather than load:** strict reps until the strict rep stops being strict, then the leg drive finishes the set. Same bell, harder first half.

**Dips go back to the angled bar.** The straight narrow bar was the experiment and it answered clearly in the other direction.

**The cable block's rotation restarts** — tri ext leads, straight-arm pulldown middle, cable lat raise last. That also keeps the cable lat raise away from the DB lateral raise, which stacked badly last week.

dayOverview.theme: The 55 gets a deliberate run. Last week's three sets at 55 came from misreading the sheet — it held, so it's the working weight now, and the only job this week is repeating it on purpose with the pack-down and the 2s eccentric intact. Push press changes shape instead of load. Dips return to the angled bar with the hand-position question closed. The cable block restarts its rotation.

spotlights.why: Two weeks of chasing palm pressure ended with a clean answer that pointed backwards: the straight narrow bar was harder generally and harder on the palms, and the angled bar 'feels more natural.' So the station question is settled and the attention moves to what dips are actually for here — a chest-biased, lean-forward press with the shoulders packed down. The lean is the variable. Sitting upright turns it into a triceps lift and puts the shoulder in the position it likes least.

It read 'much easier on grip today' last week, which on a grip-limited lift means the limiter itself moved. Worth a spotlight now because carries are about to matter more than usual — 80lb feed bags in each hand, daily, are the same movement pattern under a load nobody programmed. The gym version is where the posture gets trained: tall spine, shoulders packed down and back, ribs down, and a grip that doesn't slowly roll open.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Push spotlights: W24 incline DB + Kinesis fly · W25 dips + farmer carry (current) · W26 push press + DB lateral raise · W27 cable block. Cable-block order restarts this week (tri ext → straight-arm → lat raise) and shifts one slot per week.
watchpoints: **🔆 Dips: ANGLED / V bar.** The straight narrow bar experiment is done — it was harder on the palms and less natural. Lean forward, chest-biased, shoulders packed DOWN 🛑.
**🔆 Farmer carry: 50 per hand, 3 walks.** Tall, ribs down, shoulders packed back — the grip is the cap and it moved last week 🛑.
**Incline DB 55 across all three sets** 🛑 — the deliberate run. The pack-down and the 2s eccentric are the condition the bump was granted against.

**Push press: strict, then push press, inside ONE set.** Strict reps until the strict rep stops being strict (~4-5), then the leg drive carries it out to 8-10 🛑. Not a grind — a mechanical drop to an easier variant.
**DB lateral raise steps to 17.5**, tempo intact 🔥.
**Kinesis fly holds 9.** The step-forward ROM is the lever, not the stack 🛑.
**Cable block runs tri ext → straight-arm → lat raise.** Every lift lists a number per station — log which one you used.

**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure last set OK — DB lateral raise, cable lat raise, tri ext. 🛑 keep it shy, the cue is the cap — push press, incline DB, dips, Kinesis fly, straight-arm pulldown, farmer carry.
**Behind-back shrug goes in the warmup. Cool-down is 5 min, not optional.**

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug
sets.notes: The whole block, every push day. Yuri's band work is the shoulder anchor — don't skip it because the shoulder feels fine.

exercises.notes: Small to large. Wake the joint.
The push-day shoulder anchor. Full sequence, unhurried.
Light bell inverted. Cuff prep and grip in one — the wobble is the point.
Light opener set. Chest opener, not a working set — save the load for the spotlight block.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Primer. Shoulders packed down.
Greasing set — never to failure. Keeps the pull pattern alive on push day.
Protective activation. Behind the back, shoulders roll DOWN and back at the top.

sets.name: Push Press — Strict Until It Isn't (45) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair, 3 sets.

**The set has two halves this week:**
- **Start strict** — no leg bend, no dip. Press it with the shoulders alone
- **Keep going strict until the strict rep stops being strict** — around 4-5, you'll feel the first rep that wants a knee bend. That's the line
- **Then the leg drive finishes the set** out to 8-10 total
- **Slow eccentric on every rep**, strict or not — that's the part that's been working

**Why this instead of more weight:** it makes the first half harder without adding load, and dropping to the easier variant mid-set is a mechanical downshift, not a grind. That's what keeps it legal on a 🛑 lift.

**Pack DOWN, not up.** If the shoulders shrug toward the ears to finish a rep, that rep is over.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair.
- **Strict first** — count how many honest strict reps you get before the leg drive comes in
- **Ribs DOWN, no rib flare** at lockout
- **Slow eccentric every rep**
- **Shoulders packed DOWN**, traps relaxed

**Reflection:** how many strict reps before the first one that wanted a dip? That number is the thing to watch, not the total.

sets.name: Incline DB Press (55 Across) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 55lb pair, 3 sets of 10-12.

Three sets at 55 held last week. This is the same thing done on purpose.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 55lb pair, 3 sets.
- **Shoulder blades pinned DOWN and BACK into the bench** before the first rep — set it, then don't lose it
- **2s eccentric**, full stretch at the bottom
- **Drive with the chest**, elbows ~45° from the ribs, not flared to 90
- Last set can finish as singles if it dies — that's fine, that's what happened last week

**The condition:** 55 was granted against the pack-down and the 2s eccentric holding. If either one goes to complete a rep, the set is done.

sets.name: 🔆 Dips — Angled Bar, Chest-Biased Lean (Spotlight) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight, 3 sets of 10-12. **The ANGLED / V bar** — the station question is closed.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the lean is the lift:**
- **Lean the torso forward**, don't sit upright. Upright turns it into a triceps lift and puts the shoulder where it likes least
- **Shoulders packed DOWN at the bottom** — the shrug-up at depth is what makes dips feel bad
- **Heel of the palm takes the load**, wrists stacked over the bar, not bent back
- **Stop the descent where the chest stretch is honest**, not where the shoulder gives way — depth for its own sake isn't the goal here
- **Slow down, drive up** — the descent is where the chest work is

**Reflection:** on the angled bar with a real forward lean, where do you feel it — chest or triceps? Chest means the lean is working.

exercises.notes: **Bodyweight, 3 sets.** Angled bar. Lean forward, shoulders packed down, heel of the palm on the bar.

sets.name: DB Lateral Raise (17.5 — Keep the Tempo) 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 17.5lb, 3 sets of 12-15.

Stepped up from 15 — the tempo that made this really hard two weeks ago read 'fine, could probably go up' last week. That's the floor rising, so the load follows it.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 17.5lb.
- **Slow up, slow down, 1s hold at the top** — the tempo comes with you to the new weight
- **Lead with the elbows**, not the hands
- **Shoulders packed DOWN** — no shrug to get the last few
- Stop at shoulder height, not above

🔥 Last set can go to near failure — but the moment it turns into a shrug, it's over.

sets.name: Kinesis Cable Fly (9 — Step Forward) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 9, 3 sets of 10-12.

Holds at 9. The step forward is the progression here, not the stack.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 9.
- **Step further forward than feels necessary** — the step creates the stretch, and it's the first thing that shrinks when a fly gets easy
- **Soft elbows at a FIXED angle** — arms bending and straightening makes it a press
- **Squeeze at the midline**, slow return all the way into the stretch
- Let the bottom of the rep be the part you feel

sets.name: Cable Block — Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown → Lat Raise (3 Rounds)
sets.notes:
**Rotation restarts this week.** Tri ext leads, straight-arm middle, cable lat raise last — which also keeps the cable lat raise away from the DB lateral raise, since running them back to back stacked hard last week.

**Every lift lists a number per station. Take whichever is free and log which one you used.**

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Cable column: **70**
- Rope pulley (floor, kneeling, leaning back): **42.5**
- Kinesis: **5**

- **Elbows stay pointed forward and fixed** — only the forearms move
- **Full stretch behind the head**, then drive to lockout
- Kneeling is the default at the column station — there's no bench there

🔥 The first set always reads too easy and the last one brutal. That's the block, not a mistake — ride it.

**LOAD:**
- Cable column: **120**
- Rope pulley (kneeling, facing the stack): **62.5**

- **Arms straight the whole rep** — the moment the elbow bends it's a pulldown
- **Hinge slightly at the hips**, drive the bar to the thighs with the lats
- **Shoulders packed DOWN** before the first rep

🛑 It runs late in the session and always bites. Falling reps across sets is expected — hold the number.

**LOAD:**
- Kinesis: **5-6**
- Cable pulley + D-handle (ankle height): **9-10**
- Cable column: **~30**

- **Cable behind the body**, arm crossing in front at the bottom — that's the whole reason to do it on a cable
- **Lead with the elbow**, stop at shoulder height
- **No shrug**

🔥 Near-failure OK on the last set.

sets.name: 🔆 Farmer Carry (50 per Hand, 3 Walks — Spotlight) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb per hand, 3 walks of ~50s.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — this is a posture lift that happens to tax the grip:**
- **Stand TALL** — think of the top of the head reaching up, not the shoulders pulling back
- **Shoulders packed DOWN and BACK**, ribs down. The load wants to round you forward; don't let it
- **Grip the handle in the fingers and close the hand deliberately** — a grip that slowly rolls open is the honest end of the walk
- **Walk normally.** Short shuffling steps are a sign the load is winning
- **Breathe.** Holding your breath for 50 seconds is why carries feel harder than they are

**Reflection:** it read 'much easier on grip' last week. Is that holding, or was it a good day? And which fails first now — the grip or the posture?

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 50lb per hand, 3 walks. No straps — the grip is the lift.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout — the point is the downshift as much as the tissue.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow height.
Passive. Let the shoulders come up around the ears.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing.

tips: **Pack DOWN, not up.** On every press, raise and carry here — blades into the back pockets, neck long, traps quiet.
**The cue is the progression.** If a load can only move by breaking the cue, it's too heavy for the cue — that's the ceiling, not the number.
**Log which cable station you used**, not just the number. The scales don't convert.
